previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted from a long-term facility for fever, tachypnea, and hypotension. Initial concern was for pneumonia, but urine culture revealed Pseudomonas aeruginosa with over 100,000 organisms/mL, leading to a diagnosis of pseudomonal urosepsis. He was treated with IV Zosyn for 8 days, guided by sensitivities. Respiratory symptoms were attributed to chronic interstitial lung disease and improved with supportive care. Oral vancomycin was continued for C. diff prophylaxis. A midline was used for IV access and removed before discharge. He stabilized clinically, completed therapy, and was discharged to extended care with plans for orthopedic follow-up and medication continuation.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old male past medical history of AIDS 
complicated by multiple opportunistic infections including PCP 
and toxoplasmosis, chronic respiratory failure status post 
trach/PEG, seizure disorder, recurrent Cdiff colitis, 
lymphocytic interstitial PNA, recent hospital stay ___ for 
pseudomonal UTI, discharged on zosyn, readmitted ___ with 
acute on chronic respiratory failure, clinically improving with 
supportive treatment for aspiration pneumonitis, discharged to 
rehab.  

# Acute on Chronic Respiratory Failure / Aspiration Pneumonitis 
/ SIRS without evidence of infection / Dysphagia - Patient 
initially presented with tachycardia, tachypnea and 
leukocytosis.  Given reports from nursing home that he had 
inappropriately been taking PO (he is chronically fed via PEG, 
is NPO), there was concern for an aspiration event.  CXR 
appeared unchanged, with no indication new consolidation, and 
continued signs of chronic interstitial lung disease.  Remainder 
of infectious workup was negative. While his endotracheal 
aspirate grew gram positive and gram negative rods, he rapidly 
improved with only supportive therapy, suggesting an aspiration 
pneumonitis.  He received frequent suctioning and nebs with his 
exam resolving to baseline.  

# Osteonecrosis / Chronic Right Leg pain: Patient reported 
continued chronic right leg pain.  Imaging including xray and 
ultrasound did not reveal acute process.  Pain attributed to 
chronic changes. His pain was controlled with acetaminophen.

# Supraventricular Tachycardia - on morning of ___, patient had 
a run of 3 minutes of SVT observed on telemetry and EKG, which 
resolved with vagal maneuvers, no pharmacological intervention 
required. This is consistent with his known prior history of 
SVT. He was subsequently monitored on telemetry and continued on 
home dose of metoprolol. He had no further episodes during 
hospitalization. 

# Acute Metabolic Encephalopathy - Patient noted to be lethargic 
on morning of ___. In addition to infectious workup above, 
medications were reviewed with patient's guardian.  Per 
patient's guardian, he should not be on trazodone due to 
sedation.  Discontinued this medication (it had been on his 
nursing home medication list), and patient's mental status 
returned to baseline: opens eyes to voice, gives brief responses 
including name, and ""hospital"

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  UNILAT LOWER EXT VEINS RIGHT

INDICATION:  Evaluate for DVT in a patient with right hip pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
on the right lower extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is normal compressibility, flow and augmentation of the right common
femoral, femoral, and popliteal veins. Normal color flow and compressibility
are demonstrated in the posterior tibial and peroneal veins.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

No evidence of medial popliteal fossa (___) cyst.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the right lower extremity veins.

INDICATION:  ___ with chronic trach, p/w leukocytosis, increased sputum
production, evaluate for consolidation.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable AP chest radiograph obtained.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior chest radiographs with direct comparison made to
study from ___

FINDINGS: 

A tracheostomy tube is in unchanged position.  The lungs are unchanged in
appearance with low lung volumes and widespread bilateral hazy opacities which
likely represents a mild degree of pulmonary edema superimposed on background
chronic interstitial lung disease.  The cardiac silhouette is unchanged. 
There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION: 

Diffuse bilateral hazy opacities compatible with a combination of severe
background interstitial lung disease and a mild degree of pulmonary edema.  No
focal consolidation.  No significant interval change when compared to the
prior study.

EXAMINATION:  DX PELVIS AND HIP UNILATERAL

INDICATION:  ___ with R hip pain; chronic trach, poor mobility, evaluate for
fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  Single AP view of the pelvis with 2 additional views of the right
hip.

COMPARISON:  Pelvis radiograph from ___

FINDINGS: 

Bones are diffusely demineralized.  There is no acute fracture or dislocation.
Bilateral femoral gamma nail and intramedullary rods are noted, as well as a
transfixing screw in the right proximal femur.  There are no evidence of
hardware related complications.  Heterotopic ossification is again noted. 
There is persistent sclerosis of the bilateral femoral heads compatible with
known avascular necrosis.  Moderate degenerative changes also present at the
bilateral hips.  There is no widening of the sacroiliac joints or the pubic
symphysis.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute fracture or dislocation.  Unchanged bilateral femoral head
osteonecrosis.  No evidence of hardware related complications.
